static_traits.name: Chen Hang
static_traits.social_status: Has several close friends to confide in, but they may not fully understand the impact of commuting on their health
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems in the past; no psychotherapy received; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, fairly organized; overall attitude negative and skeptical; able to cooperate in exploration but with low expectations

basic_info.main_problem: A long daily commute overwhelms me, leading me to oversleep on rest days and thus 'ruin' my holidays.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because I noticed this pattern has had a negative impact on my overall well-being and daily routine.

core_beliefs: I cannot escape the predicament brought by commuting
My time is being wasted; life feels as if the pause button has been pressed

special_situations.event: After the workplace relocated, commute time increased to about one hour each way with traffic congestion
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I must spend a lot of time commuting every day, my life is wasted and will become miserable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: On rest days, compensating for energy by sleeping in, escaping energy-consuming activities
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is terrible; commuting makes my life miserable

special_situations.event: When rest days arrive, chooses to stay in bed for long stretches sleeping in, due to fatigue caused by absenteeism
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as I feel completely without energy, there is no recovery method other than sleeping
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces activities and going out; lies in bed all day to avoid expending energy
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I feel very tired, so I cannot do anything, can only keep sleeping

special_situations.event: Every day before work or on the way, anticipating the long commute in advance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have to commute like this every day, the whole day will be ruined and cannot be improved
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Withdraws psychologically in advance, reduces interaction with family and keeps distance to avoid conflict
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It is like this every day; there is simply no way out

special_situations.event: Already extremely exhausted on arriving at the workplace; work performance is affected
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once I am already tired before work, I cannot be competent for that day's work
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Only barely completes tasks; reduces input to conserve physical energy
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot hold on any longer; today will be awful again

core_conflict.wish: Longs to control one's time and life pace, and gain relaxation and freedom
core_conflict.fear: Fears being bound by commuting and external demands, being exhausted long-term, and relationships and work suffering
defense_goal: Maintains energy and a temporary sense of safety by avoiding activities and self-isolating (sleeping in, reducing interaction)

object_relations.self_representation: An exhausted individual who feels trapped and not understood
object_relations.object_representation: Family/others who do not understand one's predicament

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes exploring negative thinking or trying small changes (such as choosing audiobooks / podcasts)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes these attempts will not help and change is nearly impossible (transference: regarding external suggestions as futile)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Respond in a gentle, empathic tone, affirming their exhaustion and doubt; avoid arguing, invite them to choose a concrete, feasible small step and record the experience, then re-evaluate next time.

manifestations: Feeling bound by a long commute, with no way out
Believing one's life pace is controlled by external demands
outcomes: A sense of frustration and fatigue
Irritable and interacts less with family

manifestations: Every minute of driving feels like a waste
The subjective experience of 'life being on pause'

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: When discussing change, repeatedly says 'I doubt whether this is useful' and 'there will not be big changes'
Holding low expectations for attempts, cautiously accepting ('I do not have much hope')

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: On rest days, turns energy toward the self (staying in bed sleeping for long periods), rather than proactively seeking external support or changing the commuting experience
In counseling, tending more to internalize discomfort rather than discuss feasible external adjustments

positive_force: Willing to try small changes (such as listening to audiobooks/podcasts during commuting)
Proactively seeking psychological counseling, aware of the problem's negative impact on life
Having some social support (several close friends to confide in)
negative_force: Objective burden of long-distance commuting (about one hour each way, traffic congestion)
Negative cognitive patterns such as catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, and overgeneralization remain activated
Uses sleeping in as the main coping, forming a vicious cycle of fatigue - staying in bed - guilt
Holds strong skepticism about change, with an increased sense of external control (feeling 'there is no way out')
Irritable due to fatigue, affecting family relationships and work performance

target_behavior.behavior: Oversleeping / staying in bed for long periods on rest days
antecedent: Extreme fatigue and sense of 'having no energy' caused by daily long-distance commuting
target_behavior.core_reason: Emotional reasoning and energy-conservation tendency: feeling very tired and believing recovery is only possible through sleep
target_behavior.function: Avoiding unwelcome activities and energy expenditure for short-term relief of fatigue
target_behavior.consequence: Worsening burnout and guilt, decreased rest quality, decreased life satisfaction

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophic and negative expectations during and before commuting (persistent complaining and fear)
antecedent: Workplace relocation leading to longer commute time
Before work or during the commute, thinking about the one-hour drive and congestion
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing, all-or-nothing thinking, and overgeneralization cognitive patterns make commuting seem 'terrible with no way out'
target_behavior.function: Provides psychological justification for avoidance and low-investment behavior through negative expectations, and tries to gain a sense of control over emotions
target_behavior.consequence: Has already consumed a great deal of mental energy before work, causing work performance to decline and further worsening exhaustion and frustration
